input-field.name: llmBaseUrl
input-field.label: OpenAI-compatible base URL
input-field.helpText: Any OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint (Azure, OpenRouter, a local model). The URL is validated on every request to block egress into private networks; a private or loopback address is rejected.

input-field.name: llmModel
input-field.label: Model
input-field.helpText: The assistant is inert until this is set. A weak model reads as a bad product: prefer a model with reliable tool calling.

input-field.name: embeddingModel
input-field.label: Embedding model
input-field.helpText: Used to index shop documents and to match a question against them. Uses the same provider URL and API key as the chat model, so it must be a model your provider serves at /v1/embeddings. Measured working on OpenRouter: baai/bge-m3 (1024 dimensions, multilingual — the one this plugin was calibrated against), openai/text-embedding-3-small (1536) and openai/text-embedding-3-large (3072). Leave empty to switch shop information off entirely: no tool is offered to the model at all. Changing it makes every indexed document unusable — delete and index them again after a change, which the shop information screen will tell you.

input-field.name: llmApiKey
input-field.label: API key
input-field.helpText: Prefer an environment variable. Shopware system config has no real secret storage, so a key entered here is readable by anyone with config access and is included in database backups.

input-field.name: agentVoice
input-field.label: Agent voice
input-field.helpText: Tone and persona only. This text cannot grant the assistant a capability: what it may do is decided by which tools are constructed, never by instruction.

input-field.name: excludedCategories
input-field.label: Excluded category IDs
input-field.helpText: One ID per line. Products in these categories are never retrieved.

input-field.name: blockedProducts
input-field.label: Blocked product IDs
input-field.helpText: One ID per line. Blocked products never enter the model's context and never appear in a reply — the block is a retrieval filter, not a prompt instruction.

input-field.name: blockedCategories
input-field.label: Blocked category IDs
input-field.helpText: One ID per line. Same guarantee as blocked products.

input-field.name: enableAddToCart
input-field.label: Allow the assistant to add items to the cart
input-field.helpText: When off, the add-to-cart tool is never constructed, so the model cannot see it and cannot call it.

input-field.name: maxItemQuantity
input-field.label: Maximum quantity per item
input-field.helpText: Checked against the live cart, not against a single call, so repeated small additions cannot accumulate past it.

input-field.name: maxCartValue
input-field.label: Maximum cart value
input-field.helpText: In the sales channel's currency. Also checked against the live cart total.

input-field.name: maxToolCallsPerTurn
input-field.label: Maximum tool calls per turn
input-field.helpText: Bounds cost and stops a model looping. Reaching the cap ends the turn gracefully with whatever was already grounded, never with an error.

input-field.name: killSwitch
input-field.label: Kill switch — stop the assistant
input-field.helpText: Rejects every turn before any model spend, and is reported ahead of the daily cap so the trace records that the assistant was switched off rather than out of budget. The per-shopper limit still applies: switching off stops model spend, not the traffic arriving at the endpoint.

input-field.name: requestsPerMinute
input-field.label: Messages per minute, per shopper
input-field.helpText: The chat endpoint is public and every call spends model tokens, so this is the control that stops a scripted loop. Counted per caller address in a sliding window; a caller past it is refused before the shop reads or writes anything. 0 refuses every request.

input-field.name: dailyRequestCap
input-field.label: Requests per day, whole sales channel
input-field.helpText: A spend ceiling, not an abuse defence: it is the per-shopper limit above that stops one caller exhausting this. Counted in a 24-hour window that opens on the first request rather than at midnight, and reset by clearing the shop's cache. 0 refuses every request.

input-field.name: entryPointStyle
input-field.label: Entry point

option.name: Chat icon — neutral, takes your colours

input-field.helpText: Both take your colours. The chat icon is a flat mark and holds still. The character is a shaded sphere with a highlight and expressions that react to the conversation — it floats, blinks and reacts to the pointer, which is more personality than a merchant storefront usually wants. Its shading is derived from your primary colour, so it is your brand either way.

input-field.name: primaryColor
input-field.label: Primary colour
input-field.helpText: The action colour: the entry point, the send button, focus rings. Left empty, the shipped blue is used. Whatever sits on top of it is chosen automatically so it stays readable — a pale colour gets dark text, not white.

input-field.name: secondaryColor
input-field.label: Secondary colour
input-field.helpText: The quiet surface behind the assistant's replies. Deliberately not a second action colour: if two things on screen shout equally, a shopper cannot tell which one is the button.

input-field.name: enableEscalation
input-field.label: Let the assistant hand a conversation to a human
input-field.helpText: When off, the escalate tool is never constructed, so the model cannot see it and cannot call it — the same guarantee as the add-to-cart switch. The assistant then declines questions it cannot answer from shop data instead of offering a handoff.

input-field.name: escalationUrl
input-field.label: Where shoppers reach a human
input-field.helpText: A path on this shop (/contact) or an https URL. Left empty, the assistant says it cannot help with the question instead of offering a link — it never claims a human will follow up when there is nowhere to send them. Only http and https are accepted; anything else is ignored, because this link is served to every shopper.

input-field.name: escalationMessage
input-field.label: Escalation message
input-field.helpText: Shown above the link when the assistant hands off. Say what the team can help with. Left empty, a translated default is used.

input-field.name: widgetEnabled
input-field.label: Show the assistant in the storefront
input-field.helpText: When off, no entry point renders. The chat endpoint stays reachable, so a custom interface built against it keeps working. The entry point is also hidden automatically when no model is configured or the kill switch is on.

input-field.name: assistantName
input-field.label: Assistant name
input-field.helpText: Shown in the panel heading and used as its accessible name. Defaults to "Shopping Assistant".

input-field.name: greeting
input-field.label: Greeting
input-field.helpText: The first message a shopper sees. Say what the assistant can look up, not how advanced it is. Left empty, a translated default is used.

input-field.name: logTraces
input-field.label: Write one log line per conversation turn
input-field.helpText: Logs which conversation, which sales channel, how the turn ended and how long it took — and no shopper text, because a log file has neither the retention task nor the access control the conversation table has. This is the shipped example of the swag_assistant.trace_sink extension point rather than a full analytics integration: see docs/extending.md to send turns somewhere of your own.

input-field.name: traceRetentionDays
input-field.label: Keep conversations for (days)
input-field.helpText: Conversations older than this are deleted daily, together with their traces. There is no "keep forever": an empty or zero value falls back to 30 days. These rows hold what shoppers typed, so an unbounded table is a data-protection problem rather than a convenience.
